title: perf-bench-latency-throughput-taylor-ong
content:
Context / goal:
- Quick scratchpad for latency/throughput runs against rwd-llama-70b-fp16 and quantized variants on dedicated staging cluster. Trying to validate KV cache + batching heuristics and observe p50/p90/p99 tradeoffs at different concurrency points.

Environment:
- Cluster: dedicated-staging-us-west-2 (A100s, 80GB, 8-GPU pool)
- Runtime: serving-runtime v1.14.2 (local build with attention opt patch from PR 812)
- Model variants: rwd-llama-70b-fp16 (base), rwd-llama-70b-8bit (q8_0), rwd-llama-70b-4bit (q4_1)
- Sequence lengths tested: 64, 256, 1024 tokens (prompt + gen)
- Batcher: dynamic continuous-batching (default) vs fixed batch sizes (4, 8, 16)
- KV cache: enabled/disabled
- Measuring: p50/p90/p99 per-token latency (ms), tokens/sec throughput, tail latency (95/99), GPU utilization (nvidia-smi logs), mem usage

Test plan (quick):
- Baseline: fp16, KV enabled, dynamic batching, concurrency sweep: [1, 4, 8, 16, 32] at seq=256
- Quantized sweep: q8, q4 same config as baseline
- Fixed batch sweep: batch sizes 4/8/16 on q8 with KV on/off at concurrency 8
- Long sequence check: seq=1024 single-concurrency for p99 impact

Raw results (notes, approximate):
- Baseline (fp16, seq=256):
  - conc=1: p50=12ms/token, p90=16ms, p99=28ms, throughput=83 tok/s
  - conc=4: p50=13ms, p90=18ms, p99=45ms, throughput=310 tok/s
  - conc=8: p50=15ms, p90=26ms, p99=110ms, throughput=620 tok/s
  - conc=16: p50=20ms, p90=42ms, p99=220ms, throughput=900 tok/s (GPU ~85%)
  - conc=32: p50=40ms, p90=120ms, p99=420ms, throughput plateau ~920 tok/s (GPU saturated)

- Quantized q8 (seq=256):
  - conc=1: p50=9ms, p90=12ms, p99=25ms, throughput=110 tok/s
  - conc=8: p50=11ms, p90=20ms, p99=90ms, throughput=760 tok/s (GPU ~80%)
  - conc=16: p50=18ms, p90=48ms, p99=210ms, throughput=1100 tok/s (plateau)

- Quantized q4 (seq=256):
  - conc=1: p50=8ms, p90=11ms, p99=28ms, throughput=130 tok/s
  - conc=8: p50=12ms, p90=30ms, p99=160ms, throughput=820 tok/s
  - notes: q4 unstable on some long seqs (OOM-ish GC spikes) - needs mem tuning or per-layer fallback to q8.

- Fixed batch experiments (q8, concurrency=8):
  - batch=4: p50=10ms/token, throughput=520 tok/s, p99=95ms
  - batch=8: p50=12ms/token, throughput=760 tok/s, p99=120ms
  - batch=16: p50=20ms/token, throughput=960 tok/s, p99=260ms
  - takeaway: larger fixed batches increase throughput but tail latency worsens nonlinearly. For SLA p99 < 150ms, batch <=8 recommended at conc<=8.

- KV cache impact (q8, seq=256, conc=8):
  - KV enabled: p50=11ms, throughput=760 tok/s
  - KV disabled: p50=18ms, throughput=420 tok/s
  - conclusion: KV gives ~1.8x throughput improvement for workloads with prefix reuse.

- Long sequence (seq=1024, fp16, conc=1):
  - p50=28ms/token, p90=40ms, p99=110ms, throughput=36 tok/s
  - notes: attention kernel scale causes >2x per-token cost vs seq=256. Consider model chunking or early-stop heuristics for cost-sensitive apps.

Observed anomalies / jitter:
- p99 spikes at conc=8 for fp16 baseline correlated with GC/arena churn in allocator logs (attached nvidia & runtime logs). Need to repro with profiling.
- q4 OOM-like pauses only on seq>=512; didn't see on seq=256. Suspect quantization kernel memory fragmentation.

Action items / next steps:
- Re-run targeted p99 repro with cpu/gpu profiler+cuprofiler on the conc=8 fp16 case (Samir to help instrument). - due 2026-03-22
- Add fallback to q8 for layers with high memory in q4 build; test with long sequences (Maya) - due 2026-03-25
- Tune dynamic batching thresholds to cap batch size for latency-sensitive routes (experiment: set max_batch_size=8 for low-latency policy).
- Capture synthetic workload that mimics our chat route (prefix reuse patterns) and measure KV cache hit ratio precisely.

Open questions / notes to self:
- Are the attention kernel improvements from PR 812 actually the main contributor to lower p50, or is it scheduler change? Need A/B w/o patch.
- Should we expose recommended config in console for "low-latency" preset (max_batch 4, kv enabled, q8 fallback)? Good for dedicated customers.

Misc references / quick links:
- Confluence perf page: CONFLUENCE-Perf-Runs-2026
- Related GH PR: https://github.com/redwood/serving-runtime/pull/812
- Jira ticket: JIRA-PR-7891 (attention opt + batcher tuning)

Notes-to-self style (messy):
- save logs under /s3/staging/perf/taylor-2026-03-18/ (raw nvlogs + runtime traces)
- remember to tag run ids in telemetry so we can query by run in console
- if we push max_batch change, include an escape hatch (route-level override)

End of scratchpad.
